title: Process Definitions pre-assign automation status per step, marking responsible parties as automated or as human fallback
content:
Throughout the Distribution Reward Invocation chain, Required Primitive Inputs and Outputs name a Responsible Party with an automation annotation. Status transitions on the Primitive Hub Document are "Responsible party: Operational GovOps **[automated]**" (A.2.2.9.1.2.3.1.4.2, .3.2.4.2.2). Document creation and field-copying steps are "Responsible party: Operational GovOps **[if not automated]**" (A.2.2.9.1.2.3.3.3, .3.6.3). Substantive steps — the Agent drafting content, GovOps writing review feedback, the Facilitator deciding — carry no annotation and are simply human.

The pattern separates two questions the schema could have conflated: *who is accountable* for a step, and *whether a machine currently performs it*. Accountability never moves. Automation is a property of the step that can change without amending the Process Definition, because a named human fallback is already specified.

The classification is also informative on its own. Automated steps are exactly the mechanical ones — setting a status, linking a created document, inheriting a field from an approved proposal — while every step involving judgment stays unannotated. Reading the annotations tells you which parts of the Atlas are intended to become software and which are permanently human.

This is the same forward-declaration habit visible in the suspended Founder Access and Root Edit provisions: specify the target state, record the current state inline, and let implementation catch up without a document rewrite.
description: Steps are labelled "Operational GovOps [automated]" or "[if not automated]", so the same specification governs the workflow whether or not the tooling exists yet.
